equation_request.abstract: We construct a classical algorithm that designs quantum circuits for algorithmic quantum simulation of arbitrary qudit channels on fault-tolerant quantum computers within a pre-specified error tolerance with respect to diamond-norm distance. The classical algorithm is constructed by decomposing a quantum channel into a convex combination of generalized extreme channels by optimization of a set of nonlinear coupled algebraïc equations. The resultant circuit is a randomly chosen generalized extreme channel circuit whose run-time is logarithmic with respect to the error tolerance and quadratic with respect to Hilbert space dimension, which requires only a single ancillary qudit plus classical dits.

specification.problem: Given a classically specified d-dimensional qudit channel E (Choi matrix or Kraus list), classically decompose it into a convex combination of generalized extreme channels within diamond-norm error eps/2, sample one term per shot, and implement the sampled term as a Stinespring dilation on system plus one ancillary qudit, so that shot-averaged statistics approximate E(rho).
specification.reconstruction_scope: Smallest useful instance (assumed): d=2 (one system qubit) with a single ancilla qubit, i.e. 2 qubits total. The classical decomposition is taken as given or computed offline; the circuit builder implements one sampled term E_k as a unitary U_k with ancilla starting in |0>, built from standard gates (e.g. a 2-qubit unitary via the Qiskit standard-gate decomposition into CX and single-qubit gates). Outside scope: the paper's nonlinear coupled-equation solver, exact generalized-extreme-channel parametrization, the d^2 gate-count and log(1/eps) run-time proofs, fault-tolerant compilation, and general d.

symbols.domain: CPTP map on d x d matrices

symbols.meaning: Stinespring isometry of E_k, V_k|psi> = sum_j K_{k,j}|psi>|j>
unitary on system+ancilla whose action on system (x) |0> equals V_k

equations.label: Convex decomposition
equations.description: Channel written as a convex combination of generalized extreme channels, approximate within tolerance.
equations.abstract_quote: decomposing a quantum channel into a convex combination of generalized extreme channels
equations.justification: The abstract states the decomposition; the explicit error bound form is inferred from the diamond-norm tolerance claim.

equations.label: Stinespring form of each term
equations.description: Each generalized extreme channel is realized by a dilation with one ancilla qudit initialized in |0>, then discarded or measured.
equations.justification: Standard Stinespring dilation; consistent with the single-ancilla claim but the specific U_k is not given in the abstract.
assumptions: Ancilla dimension m <= d suffices (sketch assumption)
Ancilla traced out or measured with outcomes stored as classical dits

equations.label: Random-circuit average
equations.description: Sampling k with probability p_k per shot gives the mixture channel on average.
equations.abstract_quote: The resultant circuit is a randomly chosen generalized extreme channel circuit
equations.justification: A randomly chosen circuit realizes the convex combination in expectation.
assumptions: Sampling distribution is exactly p_k via classical random bits

equations.label: Error budget
equations.description: Triangle inequality and convexity of diamond norm combine decomposition and gate-synthesis errors.
equations.abstract_quote: within a pre-specified error tolerance with respect to diamond-norm distance
equations.justification: Standard norm argument supporting the stated tolerance guarantee.
assumptions: tilde E_k is the synthesized (gate-approximated) version of E_k

equations.label: Shot-averaged readout
equations.description: Measurement statistics on the system over shots with fresh k each shot approximate the target output distribution.
equations.justification: Proposed readout from the sketch; not stated in abstract.
assumptions: Pi_x projectors in the chosen measurement basis on the system register only

registers.name: sys
registers.size: ceil(log2 d) qubits (1 qubit for d=2)
registers.role: system qudit holding input rho; measured at the end

registers.name: anc
registers.size: ceil(log2 d) qubits (1 qubit for d=2)
registers.role: ancillary qudit for Stinespring dilation, starts in |0>, discarded or measured

registers.name: k_dits
registers.role: classical record of sampled index k (and optional ancilla outcomes)

specification.initial_state: rho_in on sys (a chosen input state prepared by standard gates, e.g. |0> or |+>), anc in |0>.

steps.description: Classically compute (or load) the decomposition {p_k, V_k} of E with error <= eps/2.
Per shot, sample k with probability p_k using classical random bits and store as classical dits.

Build U_k completing the isometry V_k to a unitary on sys+anc (anc in |0>) and compile with standard gates (e.g. a unitary decomposition into CX and single-qubit gates, with no initialize or dense-unitary shortcuts).
Apply U_k, then measure sys in the required basis (ancilla is traced out or measured with outcomes recorded), reset anc between shots.
Aggregate counts across shots with fresh k each; bound total error via the budget.

specification.measurement: Measure sys qubit(s) in the computational basis (or after basis-change gates); optionally measure anc. Qiskit little-endian: bits[::-1][i] is the bit set by measure(i,i).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Average counts over shots and k to estimate E(rho) statistics; no further decoding.
assumptions: Choose d=2, one system qubit plus one ancilla qubit, as the tiny instance (scope not given).
Channel is classically known (Choi/Kraus), not a black box, so no queries are used.
Nonlinear optimization is assumed to converge to a valid decomposition; it is not reconstructed.
Qudit dimension is padded to a power of 2 for qubit embedding.
Mixing is via classical sampling over shots, not coherent LCU.
Gate synthesis error is assumed bounded by eps/2.
missing_information: Exact definition of generalized extreme channels and the nonlinear coupled algebraic equations.
Explicit parametrization of U_k and the optimization procedure.
Exact gate-count and run-time derivation (log(1/eps), d^2).
How ancilla outcomes and classical dits are used within the circuit.
